sections.h2: What should a Sebastian homeowner know before selling fast?
sections.html:
A Sebastian owner choosing between a realtor, a private sale and a cash buyer should weigh the closing date and the repair list first. The city lies on the Indian River Lagoon in Indian River County, and the Census Bureau counts 85.2 percent of its homes as owner-occupied.

Most of the work is paperwork. The clerk records deeds, the tax collector bills each parcel, and the building department keeps permit files, so knowing who holds what saves days.

  • Request the permit history from the city's building department.
  • Learn whether a homestead exemption sits on the parcel.
  • Keep the deed, any survey and recent repair invoices together in one folder.

sections.h2: How did Sebastian grow into the city it is today?
sections.html:
Sebastian grew from a lagoon fishing and railroad settlement into the most populous city in Indian River County by the 2000 census. A Congressional Record tribute for the centennial recounts incorporation as a town in December 1924, then re-incorporation as a city in 1925, the same year the county was created.

Before the town had a name it was called New Haven, after a retired minister who opened its first post office. The Florida East Coast Railway arrived in the early 1890s, commercial fishing surged after a freeze in 1894, and Pelican Island became the first federal migratory bird refuge in 1903. A Miami developer bought 1,345 acres in 1957 to start Sebastian Highlands, which explains why large parts of the city are laid out in platted residential lots.

The tribute adds that health care, retail and food service lead local jobs, and that about 35 percent of residents were 65 or older.

sections.h2: What do the latest Census numbers show for Sebastian?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 27,352 residents for July 1, 2025, against 25,054 at the 2020 count, and puts the city's land area at 15.78 square miles. Residents 65 and over make up 36.8 percent of the population.

Nearly nine in ten residents stayed in the same home year over year, so Sebastian turns over slowly and many owners have held their homes for a long time. Long-held homes often carry old finishes and older permits, which is worth sorting out before an offer arrives.

sections.h2: Which Sebastian permits and repairs can slow a sale?
sections.html:
Open or expired permits are the most common permit problem, and the city building department at 1225 Main St. is where you check. Sebastian takes applications through the MGO portal and by email, and its building department phone line is 772-589-5537.

Owner-builder permits can go through the portal, but the first application has to be made in person, a requirement the city ties to Florida law. Inspections are scheduled through the portal at least one day ahead, and some air conditioning, electrical panel and plumbing inspections can be done by video.

  • Ask the building department whether any permit on your address is still open.
  • If a roof, air conditioner or water heater was replaced, find the permit and final inspection.
  • If work was done without a permit, tell the buyer or buyer's agent up front rather than at the inspection.

Cash buyers will usually take a house with unpermitted work, but they price it in. Closing out permits first can raise what a conventional buyer is willing to pay.

sections.h2: How does Indian River County taxation change at a Sebastian closing?
sections.html:
The county property appraiser assigns value as of January 1, and the tax collector bills in November. A transfer resets a capped assessment to just value the next January 1, which is why a long-time owner's low bill rarely carries to the buyer.

Florida's homestead exemption removes up to $50,000 of taxable value, and only the first $25,000 applies to school taxes. The owner files by March 1 and must have made the house a permanent residence by January 1. Renting it out or moving away ends the benefit.

Notices of proposed taxes are mailed in August. For discounts, the state prints 4 percent for November payment, 3 for December, 2 for January and 1 for February. A late-year closing means your title agent splits the year's bill between you and the buyer, so ask how they will do that. The Indian River County property appraiser can tell you which exemptions your parcel carries.

sections.h2: What do recording fees and stamp tax look like on a Sebastian deed?
sections.html:
Florida levies documentary stamp tax on the deed at 70 cents for each $100 of consideration, and the clerk collects it at recording. By the Department of Revenue's rule, each party to the deed is liable, whatever the contract says about who pays.

The clerk adds page-based fees from section 28.24 of the statutes, beginning at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for every page after, with trust fund and technology charges added. Your title agent will put the final amounts on the settlement statement.

  • Stamp tax scales with the price and any debt the buyer assumes.
  • Recording cost depends on how many pages the deed runs.
  • Mortgage payoffs, liens and unpaid taxes come out of proceeds.
  • Title charges depend on the company.

Get an itemized estimate before accepting any offer.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale suit a Sebastian owner?
sections.html:
Cash suits owners who value speed or condition over top price. With the Census Bureau counting 85.2 percent owner-occupancy and so many residents over 65, typical sellers include heirs, owners moving into assisted living and people who would rather not replace an aging roof or air handler.

Compare net proceeds, not headline numbers. A listing can bring more but adds showings, post-inspection repair requests and a longer wait. A cash buyer may pay less and still close sooner. Ask each one for the closing date, the party paying title and recording costs, and whether the offer survives their own inspection. Put the answers in writing first.

sections.h2: What should I do first if the Sebastian house is inherited or vacant?
sections.html:
Begin by confirming who has authority to sign. A house passing through an estate may need court paperwork before anyone can convey it, and the clerk of court can tell you what is filed. Keep utilities on and the yard tidy meanwhile.

Then ask the building department about permits, call the tax collector for any balance, and collect keys and association papers. With those in hand you can compare a listing with a cash buyer using real numbers.

faqs.q: Does Sebastian have its own building department?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Sebastian Building Department is at 1225 Main St. and accepts permits through the MGO portal or by email, with phone help at 772-589-5537. An owner-builder's first application must be made in person.

faqs.q: Will a buyer inherit my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The exemption follows the qualifying owner. After a sale the buyer files by March 1 for the following tax year, and the property is assessed at just value.

faqs.q: Who pays doc stamps on a Sebastian deed?
faqs.a: Every party to the deed is liable by law, and the sale contract decides who pays in practice. The clerk collects the tax at recording, at 70 cents per $100 of consideration.

faqs.q: Is a Sebastian sale still possible when permits are open?
faqs.a: Yes, with disclosure. Ask the building department which permits are open and how a buyer's title company would treat them. Cash buyers often accept open permits at a lower price.

faqs.q: What does the Census Bureau report for Sebastian home values?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes have a $317,000 median value for 2020-2024. That figure comes from a survey of owner estimates, so check recent sales near your street before pricing.
